summary: On node1, /srv/data was placed on a dedicated LVM logical volume (backed by a loop-mounted file, since the RHEL9 root disk had no volume manager). Baseline app data was written, an LVM snapshot (lv_data_snap1) was taken, the live data was then modified/corrupted/deleted, and lvconvert --merge restored /srv/data to the exact byte-for-byte baseline content (verified via sha256 checksums). A fresh snapshot (lv_data_snap_current) was left in place for ongoing recoverability, and a systemd unit (srv-data.service) ensures the loop device/VG/mount are reattached automatically on boot. Node1 was then restarted via systemctl reboot; its boot_id changed (377b5195... -> bbe2c88e...), confirming a real restart, and post-restart checks show srv-data.service active, /srv/data mounted, the snapshot LV present, and data checksums still matching the original baseline.
actions_performed: Inspected node1 disk layout (plain XFS on vda3, no LVM/Btrfs present)
Created loop-backed PV/VG (vg_srv)/LV (lv_data), formatted xfs, mounted at /srv/data
Created systemd unit srv-data.service (WantedBy=local-fs.target) to reattach loop device, activate VG, and mount /srv/data on every boot
Wrote baseline application data under /srv/data/app and recorded sha256 manifest
Created LVM snapshot lv_data_snap1 of lv_data
Modified /srv/data (corrupted/removed/added files) to simulate post-snapshot changes
Unmounted /srv/data and ran lvconvert --merge to restore lv_data from the snapshot
Remounted /srv/data and verified sha256 checksums exactly match the pre-modification baseline
Created a new snapshot lv_data_snap_current for ongoing recoverability
Captured pre-restart boot_id, service status, mount, snapshot state, and data checksums on node1
Issued a backgrounded 'sudo systemctl reboot' on node1 so the acknowledgement returned before disconnect
Polled node1 until exec connectivity returned
Verified srv-data.service active, /srv/data mounted, snapshot LV present, and data checksums matching baseline after restart

evidence.requirement: Application data under /srv/data made recoverable via filesystem snapshot (baseline capture)
evidence.summary: Baseline files written to /srv/data/app, sha256 manifest saved, and LVM snapshot lv_data_snap1 created capturing that state
record.txt corrupted, blob.bin deleted, config.conf changed, junk.txt added; checksums differ from baseline

evidence.requirement: Restore exact content captured by earlier snapshot
evidence.summary: lvconvert --merge restored lv_data from lv_data_snap1; post-restore find+sha256sum diffed against baseline.sha256 and matched exactly (MATCH_BASELINE)

evidence.requirement: Ongoing snapshot recoverability capability left in place
evidence.summary: New snapshot lv_data_snap_current created after restore so future changes remain recoverable
Captured boot_id 377b5195-..., srv-data.service active, /srv/data mounted, snapshot LV present, data checksums matching baseline
Backgrounded 'sudo systemctl reboot' returned 'reboot_issued' before the node disconnected

evidence.requirement: Node1 changed boot identity after restart
evidence.summary: Node unreachable during reboot, then exec succeeded again with new boot_id bbe2c88e-9920-4010-a535-f479ae3e8e01, differing from pre-restart value
After restart: uptime shows fresh boot, srv-data.service active, /srv/data mounted on vg_srv-lv_data, snapshot LV present, and sha256 checksums still match the original baseline manifest
